module_title: Advanced Timeline - Newly Declared National Days (Current Affairs Integration)
introduction: This advanced tier is critical for UPSC and current affairs-heavy exams. Over the last few years, the Government of India has declared several entirely new national days to honor unsung heroes, historical tragedies, and modern scientific triumphs. These are the most trending questions in recent exam cycles.

core_concepts.title: Valor and Historical Remembrance
core_concepts.description:
- **January 23: Parakram Diwas** ➡️ Declared in 2021 to mark the birth anniversary of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.
- **December 26: Veer Bal Diwas** ➡️ Declared in 2022 to commemorate the martyrdom of the four Sahibzadas (sons) of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, specifically the supreme sacrifice of Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh.

core_concepts.title: Cultural Roots and National Tragedies
core_concepts.description:
- **August 14: Partition Horrors Remembrance Day** ➡️ Declared in 2021 to acknowledge the struggles, sacrifices, and pain of millions of Indians displaced during the 1947 partition.
- **November 15: Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas** ➡️ Declared in 2021 to celebrate the birth anniversary of the great tribal freedom fighter, Bhagwan Birsa Munda.

core_concepts.title: Modern Triumphs: Space, Sports, and Environment
core_concepts.description:
- **August 23: National Space Day** ➡️ Declared in 2023 to celebrate the historic soft landing of Chandrayaan-3 on the lunar south pole (Shiv Shakti Point).
- **August 7: National Javelin Day** ➡️ Declared to honor Neeraj Chopra winning India's first Olympic gold medal in athletics at the Tokyo Olympics on August 7, 2021.
- **October 5: National Dolphin Day** ➡️ Declared in 2022 to generate awareness regarding the conservation of the Gangetic Dolphin (India's National Aquatic Animal).

important_entities.name: National Space Day (August 23)
important_entities.significance: This is currently the most high-yield static GK addition. Examiners often pair this date with the name of the landing site, **'Shiv Shakti Point'**, or the name of the rover (Pragyan) and lander (Vikram).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Children's Day vs. Veer Bal Diwas Trap
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a question asks for 'Veer Bal Diwas', do not hastily select November 14 (Jawaharlal Nehru's birthday / regular Children's Day). **Veer Bal Diwas** is exclusively **December 26**, dedicated to the Sikh Sahibzadas.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Dual Martyrs' Day (Shaheed Diwas) Confusion
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
India observes two major Martyrs' Days:
1. **January 30**: Marks the assassination of Mahatma Gandhi.
2. **March 23**: Marks the hanging of Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev. 
Read the question's context carefully to determine which one is being asked.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Throw the Javelin (7), Remember the Partition (14), Reach Space (23)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Chronologically maps the three newly declared August dates: Aug 7 (Javelin), Aug 14 (Partition Horrors), and Aug 23 (Space Day).

exam_strategy_tips: In statement-based UPSC questions, you might see assertions combining the day and the year it was declared. Pay special attention to the fact that 'Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas' (Birsa Munda's birth) and 'Parakram Diwas' were both instituted in the year 2021.
